label: Winter Storm Juno
description: NYC imposed a travel ban and shut the subway ahead of a forecast historic blizzard. The city was emptied; snowfall ultimately fell short of predictions.

label: Blizzard Jonas
description: Record nor'easter dropping ~27.5 inches in Central Park, the largest single-storm accumulation on record for NYC. A travel ban shut down roads.

label: Winter Storm Stella
description: Nor'easter forecast as a major blizzard; NYC got ~7 inches of sleet and snow. A state of emergency was declared and schools closed for two days.

label: MTA 'Summer of Hell'
description: Amtrak's emergency Penn Station repairs cut LIRR and NJ Transit service for eight weeks. The widely-feared disruption barely registered in citywide taxi demand.

label: Nor'easter Riley
description: Early-March nor'easter bringing heavy wet snow, damaging winds and coastal flooding to the NYC area.

label: COVID-19 Lockdown
description: The NYC PAUSE order halted non-essential activity from March 22. Taxi trips collapsed by roughly 90% and stayed near zero until reopening began.

label: Phase 1 Reopening
description: NYC entered Phase 1 on June 8: construction, manufacturing, wholesale and curbside retail resumed, lifting trip volume off its floor.

label: Phase 2 Reopening
description: Phase 2 began June 22: offices, in-store retail, hair salons and outdoor dining reopened, accelerating the taxi recovery.

label: Phase 3 Reopening
description: Phase 3 began July 6 with personal-care services; indoor dining was held back in NYC, slowing the recovery relative to the rest of the state.

label: Phase 4 Reopening
description: Phase 4 began July 20, the final reopening step: low-risk outdoor activity and media/entertainment resumed, with no indoor dining.

label: Winter Storm Kenan
description: A bomb-cyclone nor'easter brought blizzard conditions and close to a foot of snow to NYC, the city's biggest snowstorm in years.
